title: Class 4 automata can mimic many other systems

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Class 4 automata can mimic many other systems

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Class 4 cellular automata can, with appropriate initial conditions, mimic the behavior of all sorts of other systems, including producing unbounded growth of either complex or very simple form.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: it is a general feature of class 4 cellular automata that with appropriate initial conditions they can mimic the behavior of all sorts of other systems.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Structures in Class 4 Systems” (from p. 281), p. 291. Scope: class 4 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-24: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Universality and specific emulations are checkable for rules such as Life and rule 110. Existing proofs do not support the implication for every informally classed class 4 automaton.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For each named class 4 rule, exhibit block encodings or computational constructions that simulate target systems, and use universality proofs where available. Define a target-system family before quantifying how broadly mimicry extends.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Encoding constructions may be highly specialized.

Class 4 does not automatically imply computational universality.

“All sorts” is not a quantified target class.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.62
data existence: 0.92
data adequacy: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Specific growing seeds are described well enough to resimulate, and a repeating production cycle can turn some of them into proofs of unbounded growth. The sentence says class 4 automata can mimic all sorts of other systems, which those seeds illustrate and do not exhaust. Existing simulators resolve the examples and leave the general feature as a sample.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-run the published seeds for unbounded growth in rule 110 and in the code 1329 rule, and prove growth from a repeating production cycle where one exists. A seed whose pattern provably grows supports that example; all sorts of other systems has no fixed target list.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A long growing run is not yet a proof of unbounded growth.

The general class 4 claim is much wider than rule 110 and code 1329.

All sorts of other systems is not a fixed list of target behaviors.
